subject: maths
title: Multiplication and Division Strategies
seo_title: Year 4 Multiplication and Division Strategies Worksheets: Partitioning, Area Model, Short Multiplication (Free)
standard_text: Develop efficient strategies and use appropriate digital tools for solving problems involving addition and subtraction, and multiplication and division where there is no remainder
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on multiplication and division strategies, following the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N06): partitioning 2- and 3-digit numbers, the area model, short multiplication, dividing by partitioning and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Partition the number into parts you know. Multiply or divide every part, then add the answers.
body_html:
Use the facts you know

You know 4 × 6 = 24. So 40 × 6 is 4 tens × 6 = 24 tens = 240. And 400 × 6 is 24 hundreds = 2400. Division works the same way: 80 ÷ 4 is 8 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens = 20.

Multiply by partitioning

Partition the bigger number into hundreds, tens and ones. Multiply every part. Then add the parts.

3-digit × 1-digit

236 × 4 = ?

236 = 200 + 30 + 6. 200 × 4 = 800, 30 × 4 = 120 and 6 × 4 = 24. Add: 800 + 120 + 24 = 944.

Answer: 944

Short multiplication

Short multiplication is the same idea written in columns. Start with the ones. If a product is 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup the tens into the next column.

Divide by partitioning

Partition the number into parts that divide equally. Divide each part, then add the answers.

When the tens do not divide equally

72 ÷ 4 = ?

7 tens do not divide equally by 4. Use 72 = 40 + 32. 40 ÷ 4 = 10 and 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Add: 10 + 8 = 18. Check: 18 × 4 = 72.

Answer: 18

Always check a division with multiplication. Multiplication and division are inverse operations.

Equal groups, sharing and arrays

Equal groups or rows in an array: multiply. Sharing equally or making equal groups from a total: divide.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to multiply the tens (34 × 6 = 30 + 24 = 54)Multiply every part: 30 × 6 = 180, so 180 + 24 = 204
Place value slip (30 × 6 = 18)30 × 6 = 3 tens × 6 = 18 tens = 180
Forgetting the regrouped digit (47 × 6 = 242)Add the regrouped 4: 4 × 6 + 4 = 28, so 282
Dividing only one part (84 ÷ 4 = 20 + 4 = 24)Divide both parts: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 and 4 ÷ 4 = 1, so 21
Splitting into parts that do not divide (72 = 70 + 2 for ÷ 4)Choose 72 = 40 + 32. Both parts divide by 4

faq.q: What multiplication strategies do Year 4 students learn in Australia?
faq.a: Year 4 students use their multiplication facts with partitioning, the area model and short multiplication. For 34 × 6 they work out 30 × 6 = 180 and 4 × 6 = 24, then add to get 204.

faq.q: How do you divide by partitioning?
faq.a: Split the number into parts that each divide equally, divide each part and add the answers. For 84 ÷ 4, use 80 ÷ 4 = 20 and 4 ÷ 4 = 1, so the answer is 21.

faq.q: Do Year 4 students learn division with remainders?
faq.a: The Year 4 Australian Curriculum content description (AC9M4N06) focuses on division where there is no remainder. Remainders are met in Year 3 and studied further in Year 5.
No. NAPLAN is for Years 3, 5, 7 and 9. The multiplication and division strategies learnt in Year 4 are the base for the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test.

sets.title: Dividing by partitioning and known facts

items.q: What is 210 ÷ 7? Think: 21 ÷ 7 = 3.
items.e: 210 is 21 tens. 21 tens ÷ 7 = 3 tens = 30. Not 3: the answer is tens, not ones. Check: 30 × 7 = 210.

items.q: 96 is partitioned like this. What is 96 ÷ 3?
items.e: Partition 96 = 90 + 6. 90 ÷ 3 = 30 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Add: 30 + 2 = 32. Check: 32 × 3 = 96. Divide both parts, not just the first.

items.q: What is 240 ÷ 6? Think: 24 ÷ 6 = 4.
items.e: 240 is 24 tens. 24 tens ÷ 6 = 4 tens = 40. Not 4: the answer is tens, not ones. Check: 40 × 6 = 240.

items.q: What is 856 ÷ 8?
items.e: Partition 856 = 800 + 56. 800 ÷ 8 = 100 and 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Add: 100 + 7 = 107. Check: 107 × 8 = 856. The answer has 0 tens, so it is 107, not 17.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ ÷ 4 = 23
items.e: Use the inverse: ☐ = 23 × 4 = 80 + 12 = 92. Check: 92 ÷ 4 = 23. (27 is 23 + 4. 82 forgets the ten in 12.)

items.q: 72 is partitioned like this. What is 72 ÷ 4?
items.e: 7 tens do not divide equally by 4, so partition into parts that do. Partition 72 = 40 + 32. 40 ÷ 4 = 10 and 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Add: 10 + 8 = 18. Check: 18 × 4 = 72. Divide both parts, not just the first.

items.q: Which split makes 72 ÷ 4 easy to work out?
items.e: Both parts must divide equally by 4. 40 ÷ 4 = 10 and 32 ÷ 4 = 8, so 72 ÷ 4 = 18. In the other splits, at least one part does not divide equally by 4.

items.q: Which split makes 84 ÷ 6 easy to work out?
items.e: Both parts must divide equally by 6. 60 ÷ 6 = 10 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so 84 ÷ 6 = 14. In the other splits, at least one part does not divide equally by 6.

items.q: Which split makes 92 ÷ 4 easy to work out?
items.e: Both parts must divide equally by 4. 80 ÷ 4 = 20 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so 92 ÷ 4 = 23. In the other splits, at least one part does not divide equally by 4.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 7 × ☐ = 84
items.e: Use the inverse: ☐ = 84 ÷ 7. Partition 84 = 70 + 14. 70 ÷ 7 = 10 and 14 ÷ 7 = 2, so ☐ = 12. Check: 7 × 12 = 84.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 96 ÷ ☐ = 32
What is 369 ÷ 3?
What is 78 ÷ 6?
items.e: 7 tens do not divide equally by 6, so partition into parts that do. Partition 78 = 60 + 18. 60 ÷ 6 = 10 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3. Add: 10 + 3 = 13. Check: 13 × 6 = 78. Divide both parts, not just the first.

items.q: What is 85 ÷ 5?
items.e: 8 tens do not divide equally by 5, so partition into parts that do. Partition 85 = 50 + 35. 50 ÷ 5 = 10 and 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Add: 10 + 7 = 17. Check: 17 × 5 = 85. Divide both parts, not just the first.

items.q: What is 484 ÷ 4?
Which split makes 91 ÷ 7 easy to work out?
items.e: Both parts must divide equally by 7. 70 ÷ 7 = 10 and 21 ÷ 7 = 3, so 91 ÷ 7 = 13. In the other splits, at least one part does not divide equally by 7.

items.q: What is 80 ÷ 4? Think: 8 ÷ 4 = 2.
items.e: 80 is 8 tens. 8 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens = 20. Not 2: the answer is tens, not ones. Check: 20 × 4 = 80.

items.q: 84 is partitioned like this. What is 84 ÷ 4?
items.e: Partition 84 = 80 + 4. 80 ÷ 4 = 20 and 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Add: 20 + 1 = 21. Check: 21 × 4 = 84. Divide both parts, not just the first.

items.q: What is 150 ÷ 5? Think: 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
items.e: 150 is 15 tens. 15 tens ÷ 5 = 3 tens = 30. Not 3: the answer is tens, not ones. Check: 30 × 5 = 150.

items.q: 91 is partitioned like this. What is 91 ÷ 7?
items.e: 9 tens do not divide equally by 7, so partition into parts that do. Partition 91 = 70 + 21. 70 ÷ 7 = 10 and 21 ÷ 7 = 3. Add: 10 + 3 = 13. Check: 13 × 7 = 91. Divide both parts, not just the first.

items.q: Mei runs 4 laps of a 400 m running track. How far does she run?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 400 × 4. 4 hundreds × 4 = 16 hundreds. The answer is 1600 m.

items.q: A netball costs $18. The school buys 7 netballs. How much do they cost altogether?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 18 × 7. Partition 18 = 10 + 8. 10 × 7 = 70. 8 × 7 = 56. Add: 70 + 56 = 126. The answer is $126.

items.q: A box holds 24 muesli bars. The school canteen buys 6 boxes. How many muesli bars is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 24 × 6. Partition 24 = 20 + 4. 20 × 6 = 120. 4 × 6 = 24. Add: 120 + 24 = 144. The answer is 144 muesli bars.

items.q: 96 oranges are packed into bags of 6. How many bags are filled?
items.e: Making groups of 6, so divide: 96 ÷ 6. Partition 96 = 60 + 36. 60 ÷ 6 = 10 and 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Add: 10 + 6 = 16. Check: 16 × 6 = 96.

items.q: At the swimming carnival the seats are in 8 rows. Each row has 35 seats. How many seats are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 35 × 8. Partition 35 = 30 + 5. 30 × 8 = 240. 5 × 8 = 40. Add: 240 + 40 = 280. The answer is 280 seats.

items.q: Three friends share the cost of a $54 present equally. How much does each friend pay?
items.e: Sharing equally, so divide: 54 ÷ 3. Partition 54 = 30 + 24. 30 ÷ 3 = 10 and 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Add: 10 + 8 = 18. Check: 18 × 3 = 54.

items.q: A school vegetable garden has 6 rows of carrots. Each row has 48 carrots. How many carrots are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 48 × 6. Partition 48 = 40 + 8. 40 × 6 = 240. 8 × 6 = 48. Add: 240 + 48 = 288. The answer is 288 carrots.

items.q: The 128 students in Year 4 line up in 4 equal lines. How many students are in each line?
items.e: Sharing equally, so divide: 128 ÷ 4. Partition 128 = 120 + 8. 120 ÷ 4 = 30 and 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Add: 30 + 2 = 32. Check: 32 × 4 = 128.

items.q: Sausages come in packs of 8. The school buys 45 packs for the sausage sizzle. How many sausages is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 45 × 8. Partition 45 = 40 + 5. 40 × 8 = 320. 5 × 8 = 40. Add: 320 + 40 = 360. The answer is 360 sausages.

items.q: Isla has 6 packets of 24 stickers. She shares all the stickers equally among 4 friends. How many stickers does each friend get?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 24 = 120 + 24 = 144 stickers. Step 2: 144 ÷ 4. Partition 144 = 120 + 24. 120 ÷ 4 = 30 and 24 ÷ 4 = 6, so each friend gets 36. Check: 36 × 4 = 144. (54 forgets to divide the 24.)

items.q: A 72 cm ribbon is cut into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Sharing equally, so divide: 72 ÷ 3. Partition 72 = 60 + 12. 60 ÷ 3 = 20 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Add: 20 + 4 = 24. Check: 24 × 3 = 72.

items.q: 91 chairs are set out in 7 equal rows for assembly. How many chairs are in each row?
items.e: Sharing equally, so divide: 91 ÷ 7. Partition 91 = 70 + 21. 70 ÷ 7 = 10 and 21 ÷ 7 = 3. Add: 10 + 3 = 13. Check: 13 × 7 = 91.

items.q: 84 students are split equally into 4 sport houses. How many students are in each house?
items.e: Sharing equally, so divide: 84 ÷ 4. Partition 84 = 80 + 4. 80 ÷ 4 = 20 and 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Add: 20 + 1 = 21. Check: 21 × 4 = 84.

items.q: Jack buys 4 pies at the school canteen. Each pie costs $5. He pays with a $50 note. How much change does he get?
items.e: Step 1: cost: 4 × $5 = $20. Step 2: change: $50 − $20 = $30. ($20 is the cost, not the change.)

items.q: The school hall has 9 rows of chairs with 26 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 26 × 9. Partition 26 = 20 + 6. 20 × 9 = 180. 6 × 9 = 54. Add: 180 + 54 = 234. The answer is 234 chairs.

items.q: Liam reads 8 pages each night. How many nights does it take him to read a 96-page book?
items.e: Making groups of 8, so divide: 96 ÷ 8. Partition 96 = 80 + 16. 80 ÷ 8 = 10 and 16 ÷ 8 = 2. Add: 10 + 2 = 12. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: Tickets to the school concert cost $8 each. The class sells 136 tickets. How much money is that?
Three buses take Year 4 on a school excursion. Each bus has 57 seats. How many seats is that altogether?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 57 × 3. Partition 57 = 50 + 7. 50 × 3 = 150. 7 × 3 = 21. Add: 150 + 21 = 171. The answer is 171 seats.

items.q: For assembly there are 5 rows of 16 chairs and 3 rows of 12 chairs. How many chairs are there?
Each class at the athletics carnival has 27 students. There are 5 classes. How many students is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 27 × 5. Partition 27 = 20 + 7. 20 × 5 = 100. 7 × 5 = 35. Add: 100 + 35 = 135. The answer is 135 students.
